quote: Geg. eine ternäre Form 4ter Ordnung gesucht 3 ternäre quadra= tische Formen, so dass $f = \varphi\psi - \chi^2$ (Problem der Doppeltangenten einer Curve 4ter Ordnung.)
english: Given a ternary form of 4th order, find 3 ternary quadratic forms such that f = φψ − χ² (problem of the bitangents of a curve of 4th order).
topic: Notes on superfluous invariants of binary forms, on computing the characteristic function for ternary forms (in particular expressing a ternary quartic as $\varphi\psi-\chi^2$, the bitangent problem), and on extending the Cayley-Sylvester counting theorem to ternary forms.

triage.modern_statement: Given a ternary quartic form f (a plane quartic curve C ⊂ P^2), find ternary quadratic forms φ, ψ, χ with f = φψ − χ². Geometrically, the conics φ=0 and ψ=0 each meet C in 4 points of tangency (C is tangent to each conic there), and the pencil φ + 2tχ + t²ψ gives a family of conics that are 4-fold tangent to C. Every pair of bitangents belonging to the same Steiner complex gives a degenerate member of this family. Over C this is the same as writing f = q1² + q2² + q3², because q1² + q2² = (q1 + i q2)(q1 − i q2). The questions are whether such representations exist, how many inequivalent ones there are, and how to compute them, which ties the problem to the 28 bitangents.
triage.answered_by: The existence and count were settled classically in the 19th century. Bitangent theory goes back to Plücker and Jacobi, and Hesse, Steiner, Aronhold and Cayley developed Steiner complexes and Cayley octads, though no source I found ties a specific name or date to the φψ − χ² statement itself. Result: a smooth plane quartic has exactly 63 inequivalent representations f = φψ − χ² (equivalently, as a sum of three squares), one for each of the 63 Steiner complexes of bitangents. Exact algorithms that compute these representations from the 28 bitangents are in D. Plaumann, B. Sturmfels and C. Vinzant, 'Quartic curves and their bitangents', J. Symbolic Computation 46 (2011) 712–733, arXiv:1008.4104.

evidence.claim: A smooth complex plane quartic has 36 inequivalent representations as a symmetric determinant of linear forms and 63 representations as a sum of three squares. These correspond to Cayley octads and Steiner complexes, and exact algorithms compute them from the 28 bitangents.
It is described as known that a smooth ternary quartic can always be written as q1² + q2² + q3², in exactly 63 nonequivalent ways (citing Dolgachev-style classical references).
Every plane quartic has 28 bitangents (Plücker, Jacobi). Related structures such as Cayley octads, Aronhold heptads and Steiner complexes were found in the 19th century.

triage.why: Over C, φψ − χ² and a sum of three squares are equivalent forms, and the existence of such representations and their number (63, matching the Steiner complexes) were classical results by Hilbert's time. The note looks like a standard problem Hilbert wrote down, not a new open question, and it is not among his published problems. The topic is still being studied: computational and real-algebraic work (Plaumann–Sturmfels–Vinzant 2011, on spectrahedra and Gram matrices of positive quartics) and arithmetic and topological work (a 2023 paper in the European Journal of Mathematics) are recent. No source I found addresses Hilbert's notebook entry directly, so linking the note to these results is my own reading of the mathematics.
